CITY OF ALHAMBRA

  NOTICE OF REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE
  ALHAMBRA ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY
  COMMISSION
  THURSDAY, MARCH 13, 2025
  6:00 p.m.

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that a Regular Meeting of the Alhambra
Environmental Sustainability Commission will be held on Thursday, March
13, 2025 at 6:00 p.m. in Conference Room A, on the second floor of the
Alhambra City Hall, 111 S. First St., Alhambra, California, pursuant to the
order of the Alhambra Environmental Sustainability Commission Secretary.

An agenda of such regular meeting is attached hereto, incorporated herein by
reference and made a part hereof as though fully set forth herein.

  Latoya Waters,
  Alhambra Environmental Sustainability
  Commission Secretary

Notice No. N2M25-27
Posted: 03/06/2025
   CITY OF ALHAMBRA
  AGENDA
  REGULAR MEETING
  ALHAMBRA ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY COMMISSION

  City Hall, 111 South First Street
  March 13, 2025
  6:00 p.m.

  I.  ROLL CALL
  Lisa Massaro, Amy Wong, Katie Chan, Scott Chan, Xana Hermosillo

  II.  ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY MEETING MINUTES
  Commission Members will vote to approve 11-14-24 meeting minutes.
  Recommended Action: Approve the meeting minutes.

  III.  ELECTION OF OFFICERS
  At this time, it is appropriate to conduct an election to determine which member will chair the
  meeting as President. Should the current Vice President be elected as President, the
  Commissioners shall elect a Vice President.
  Recommended Action: Commission to elect a new President.

  IV.  SUSTAINABILITY PLAN UPDATE
  Staff will provide an update on the Sustainability Plan.
  Recommended Action: Information only. No action required

  V.  ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY PLAN DISCUSSION
  The Environmental Sustainability Commission will discuss action items for the next meeting.
  Recommended Action: Information and discussion. No action required.

  VI.  PUBLIC COMMENT
  Discussion from the public of any item not specified on the agenda. Comments are welcome, but
  must pertain to the business of the Alhambra Environmental Sustainability Commission. Please limit
  all oral communication to five (5) minutes. Speakers must fill out a blue speaker’s card, prior to the
  meeting and submit it to the Commission Secretary. Comments must pertain to the business of the
  Environmental Sustainability Commission. Please limit all oral communications to five (5) minutes.

  VII.  COMMISSION COMMUNICATION
  Discussion from the Commission Members of any item not specified on the agenda and agenda
  items for next meeting. Items must pertain to the business of the Alhambra Environmental
  Sustainability Commission.
  Recommended Action: Discussion only. No action required.

  VIII.  ADJOURNMENT
  Adjournment to the next regular meeting on Thursday, May 8, 2025 at 6:00 p.m.

3/13/2025
 If you wish to address the Commission during the meeting, please complete a speaker’s card and give it to
the secretary. When making your presentation, please give your name and address for the record. Please
make your statement as brief as possible. The maximum time for addressing the Committee is five minutes.

If you wish to address the Commission on an item which appears on the agenda, your comments will be
heard during the Commission’s discussion of that item. If you wish to address the Committee on a subject
which does not appear on the agenda, but is of an environmental concern, your comments will be heard
under Public Comments. Please be advised that under the State of California’s Ralph M. Brown Act, the
Commission cannot take action on any item which does not appear on the agenda.

Copies of staff reports or other written documentation, if any, relating to each item of business described
above are on file in the Alhambra City Hall, Public Works Department, 111 S. First Street, Alhambra
California 91801 and are available for public inspection upon request during regular business hours of
7:00am to 5:30pm, Monday through Thursday.

Should any person have a question concerning any of the above agenda items prior to the meeting
described herein, he or she may contact Latoya Waters, Deputy Director of Utilities, either in person at the
Utilities Department at Alhambra City Hall, 111 South First Street, or by calling via telephone at (626) 570-
5067 during regular business hours.

  MINUTES
  Environmental Sustainability Commission
  Regular Meeting on November 14, 2024

  The regular meeting of the Environmental Sustainability Commission was called to
  order at 6:00 p.m. on November 14, 2024.

  I.  Roll Call
  Commission Members Present: Massaro, Chan, Hermosillo

  Commission Members Absent: Wong, Sahu

  Staff Present:  David Dolphin – Commission Secretary
  Latoya Waters – Environmental Compliance Specialist
  Lucy Garcia – Assistant City Manager

  Members of the Public:

  Lola Armendariz
  Sandy Lee

  In the absence of Commissioner Sahu, Commissioner Hermosillo prepared to chair the meeting
  and review the agenda items.

 II.  VOTE TO APPROVE MEETING MINUTES
  Commissioner Chan motioned to approve the meeting minutes from September 9, 2024.
  Commissioner Massaro seconded the motion.

  Motion to approve meeting minutes passed.

III.  SUSTAINABILITY PLAN UPDATE
  Provided in the Agenda packets and verbally presented by City staff:

  Sustainability Plan: Presented by Lucy Garcia – Assistant City Manager
  The City’s new Sustainability Analyst, Katie Martel will have a more focused role on
  sustainability and will be working regularly with the Environmental Commission and City Staff
  on updates to the plan. The consultant provided an overview at the previous meeting. This next
  phase (Strategy Development) involves input from the community and collection of “actionable
  items” such as expanding green space. The Sustainability Analyst and Sustainability Consultants
  (Team) are engaged in continual conversations with community groups.
  There was initial consideration for townhall meetings in November, but the meetings have been
  postponed until January to accommodate elections and holiday schedules. Five (5) townhall

  Page 1 of 6
   ITEM #II
meetings will be scheduled, one (1) per district. These meetings have not been formally
scheduled. In the meantime, the Team has tabled at community events such as the “Pumpkin
Run” to talk to community members about Sustainability. A tool utilized at the “Pumpkin Run”
was a postcard to open conversations by asking “What does Sustainability in Alhambra look like
to you?”, regardless of demographics or background.
A few of the aforementioned postcards collected were presented to the Commissioners and
meeting attendees. Some of the postcards read:
    “I’d like to see signs in different languages promoting a clean community”
    “More community outreach and better pick up on trash days”
    “Fruit trees and exercise equipment at each park “
    In Spanish “Necesitamos mas arboles para mejor aire”
  o Translated: “We need more trees for better air”
    A picture was drawn by a young community member demonstrating trees, butterflies, and
  identified the need for a community garden, compost, and labeled various vegetables.
    A picture drawn to depict the need for a clean world.
    Another picture was drawn and read “Please don’t litter”
Just to provide a sense of how the community thinks about Sustainability and make connections
to community members. Data collected will be added to the data center for prioritization. These
are the highlights that matter because the Team can see for example, if trees are a common
theme, trees can rise to the top of the priority list of actionable items that City Council may want
to address. The Team also has data from community groups such as Asian Pacific Islander
Forward Movement (APIFM).

One notable comment from the Commissioners was to make the outreach more intentional. With
this feedback the Team has taken the time to speak to groups such as Active San Gabriel Valley
(Active SGV) and APIFM who have already built relationships with community members and
are having discussions about the environmental community. In speaking to the aforementioned
groups, the Team was also looking for critical assessment of the Team’s approach, as well as
exploring potential partnership opportunities.

Again, during the month of January (dates have not been advertised) the City will look for more
feedback with a townhall type meeting. Once solidified the dates will be shared with the
Commissioners. There is a lot of alignment with other plans (Bike and Pedestrian Improvement
Plan, Hazard Mitigation Plan) where there are some sustainability connections. Looking to
capture as many opportunities as possible to make the strategies viable. Any questions?

Question and Comment: Lola Armendariz – what kind of community outreach do you do? In
what manner? There have been quite a few council meetings under oral communications, in the
last page of the Agenda there used to be a list of upcoming events. It is an ongoing request.

  Page 2 of 6
   ITEM #II

Lucy Garcia - The consultant is aware of all calendar events to the extent that Staff can be
present and table at these events.

Lola Armendariz – I would like to see something from Council.

Lucy Garcia – The sustainability team made presentations to Council to keep them abreast where
we are in the planned development phase. As we move through the strategy development,
Council will receive another update. Keep in mind once we move through these phases, we will
be in the draft of the plan and there will be another opportunity to comment.

Commissioner Hermosillo – I would add if you want to look at the minutes from the last
meeting, a lot of the Commissioners gave feedback on ways we would like to see outreach
happening, we shared some of your same concerns. They will try to move forward with a lot of
the suggestions we provided.

Lola Armendariz – another way of doing it is to post on the windows downstairs [City Hall].
Even at the counters, the information counters [City Hall]. One thing I suggested in the past, is a
kiosk, like the one in the Police Department that holds the agendas for Planning Commission and
City Council; since that is a 24-hour facility and there’s probably more activity in that lobby than
there is in ours [City Hall lobby]. Not sure if the high school students are restricted from passing
through the [City Hall] lobby but at one point they would just pass through, they may be
interested if there is a kiosk. It would be a good way to get the students involved.

Lucy Garcia– Yes, we are establishing outreach to students as well because we recognize how
important that is.

Lola Armendariz – I am not a social media person; I like to pick up a hardcopy and read through
at my leisure.

Commissioner Hermosillo – is it possible once the January [townhall meeting] dates are set to
publish it in “Around Alhambra”?

Lucy Garcia– That is not the City’s publication we would be able to catch some of it in the
Recreational Newsletter. We also have our own electronic newsletter. Part of the advantage of
the card [“What does Sustainability in Alhambra look like to you?” postcard], was that we were
getting registration information so for people wanting to opt in and learn more about
sustainability, they became part of our database and we are sending information that way as well.
We can utilize a variety of options to further engage people.

David Dolphin – didn’t we have flyers last time?

Lucy Garcia– Yes, we did. I think one of the things for the first phase, was to meet people where
there are. We went to parks and tabled at the corner of Garfield and Main Street as people were
hopping on the bus. Some people were busy exercising or rushing to get on the bus, we certainly

  Page 3 of 6
   ITEM #II
respected that. We tried different strategies, of course are doing multilingual and all the more
reason to reach out to the community-based groups that are successful in these engagements
really matters to us and will make a substantial difference to our outreach efforts.

Commissioner Hermosillo - any other public comments? Fellow Commissioners, comments?

Commissioner Chan – yes. I am glad you are moving it [Public Meeting] to January, gives more
time for planning and outreach. Are you planning to have one (1) per district? Are they going to
be at churches?

Lucy Garcia– We have not determined the locations, traditionally we have had some meetings
here at Reese Hall, Jocelyn Center, we have had some at Almansor Park. One of our first
outreach events was outside in the park and subsequently at the gym. We want to try different
locations where people can conveniently stop-by and participate. We are scouting locations right
now. Any recommendations are appreciated.

Commissioner Chan – Yes. Definitely consider Almansor Park.

David Dolphin – Yes, there are schools in each district.

Commissioner Chan – I think that is good. I like that you are doing things in multilingual. Are
there any multilingual postcards?

Lucy Garcia– No. That is a good suggestion. We do have facilitators that are tabling, they are
multilingual.

Lola Armendariz – Who is going to be available at the townhall meetings to assist with
multilingual?

Lucy Garcia– The consultant will provide translators. Facilitators for primary languages in
Alhambra (Spanish and Mandarin). We are still working on the second phase of strategy
development.

Commissioner Massaro – When we have events (Pumpkin Run) with food. I went to an event at
the Rose Bowl (with Sandy Lee) and the vendors were recycling scraps. Will they do that in
Alhambra?

Lucy Garcia– Yes. part of our requirements under SB1383 is food recovery. At the Farmer’s
Market there’s a whole program in place to facilitate food recovery.

Commissioner Hermosillo – one last thing I would like to add: someone asked about trash
pickup. Trash rates were raised to accommodate bulky item pickups. However, bulky items are
not being picked up. If there is a way to check-in with Republic?

  Page 4 of 6
   ITEM #II
  Lucy Garcia– in the event you experience that again, contact us here in the office as we have
  direct contact with Republic.

IV.  ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY PLAN DISCUSSION
  Placed on the agenda to allow the Commissioners to discuss, if necessary.

  Commissioner Chan – There is not that much for us to work with right now. As we get closer to
  January sessions, we will have more things to talk about and advise on.

  Commissioner Hermosillo – What does it look like for commissioners to provide
  recommendations and actions?

  David Dolphin – You all are an advisory commission for the City Council; to put forth
  recommendations to Council members. As well as partake in the development of the plan(s).

  Lucy Garcia– You will have opportunity to convey your thoughts or impressions as we move
  forward.

  Commissioner Chan – We decide as a group and provide to you all (City Staff)?

  Lucy Garcia– In an advisory capacity we (City Staff) present the information and include it in
  the presentation to Council.

  Commissioner Hermosillo – Multiple organizations are requesting money for tree planting. How
  do we encourage the City to coordinate with Active SGV for tree planting?

  Lucy Garcia– We are well aware that Active SGV has applied for these grants and there is an
  award of funds available. The details have not been shared with the City. If it is a private
  giveaway event, this may not involve the City directly. We can definitely get more information
  to the Commissioners.

  Commissioner Hermosillo – Will our next agenda look like it is now?

  David Dolphin – it does not have to be decided now, we can communicate via email to finalize
  the next agenda.

V.  PUBLIC COMMENT

  Speaker card: Lola Armendariz – What are you speaking of regarding trees? Is there something
  in progress regarding tree planting and purchasing?

  Commissioner Hermosillo – No. Active SGV released some information regarding trees in
  communities such as Alhambra. Asking if this is something the City will pursue.

  Lola Armendariz – further general comments:
   Ficus tree removal along Main Street “Auto Row”, exposed tree roots, trees needing to be
  watered, and too much trimming on Alhambra Park trees.

  Page 5 of 6
   ITEM #II
    Bike plan proposed along Alhambra Rd. to remove center lane from Atlantic to
  Huntington Dr. all of the residents are not informed of this proposal.
    Residents immediately affected by “T intersections” should directly be contacted.
    On pg. 5 of the minutes – Safe Clean Water Program at Burke Park
  o Why are the two (2) smallest parks in the community selected to capture water?
  o The proposed playground will affect those living in the apartments near Burk
  Heritage Park.
  o Why are they holding watch commander meetings when people no longer want
  them in their homes?
  o Some things attached to Environmental Sustainability like historic preservation.
    On pg. 9 – grass
  o Grass is the biggest oxygen producer.
  o Taking out grass and replacing it with native vegetation was a thought when we
  did not have the population and oxygen demand we now have.
  o Why do we have to increase trees on private property?
    David Dolphin –
  o He is retiring in January 2025 and this is his last meeting.
    Well wishes and congratulations shared from attendees.

VI.  COMMISSION COMMUNICATION

  No further Commissioner communication.

VII.  ADJOURNMENT
  Commissioner Hermosillo motioned to adjourn the meeting at 6:53 PM.
